inputs.note: FY2025 actuals (year ended 31 December 2025). Revenue ~$440m, EBITDA ~$96m, NPBT ~$48m, NPAT $32m, EPS $0.76. Net bank debt confirmed $100.3m at December 2025. OCF estimated at ~$75m (EBITDA $96m less cash tax ~$12m, cash interest ~$9m). Equity ~$290m is December 2025 estimate (H1-2025 equity $302m less H2 loss and October 2025 dividend). Cash approximated from H1-2025 balance sheet.

historical_growth.revenue_calculation_note: 3yr: FY2022 $348.4m to FY2025 $440.0m over 3 years. 5yr: FY2020 $251.5m to FY2025 $440.0m over 5 years. FY2023 anomaly (Cyclone Gabrielle, $301m) falls in the middle window but CAGR uses start/end endpoints only.
historical_growth.eps_calculation_note: 3yr: FY2022 EPS $0.16 to FY2025 $0.76 - highly distorted by FY2022 low margins from volume softness. 5yr: FY2020 $0.52 to FY2025 $0.76 = 7.9% CAGR, more meaningful as both are normal-volume years. EPS volatile due to operating leverage and one-off tax items (FY2024 had $12.5m deferred tax charge).
historical_growth.equity_calculation_note: 3yr: FY2022 equity $270.9m to FY2025 est. $290m over 3 years = 2.3% - depressed by FY2023 loss ($14.5m) and dividend payments. 5yr: FY2020 $176.3m to FY2025 $290m over 5 years = 10.5% CAGR. The 5yr rate better reflects the business's sustained value creation through the cycle.
historical_growth.fcf_calculation_note: Using Operating Cash Flow as FCF proxy (minimal maintenance capex given existing 50m+ tray capacity). 3yr: FY2022 $12.1m to FY2025 $75.0m - severely distorted by anomalous FY2022 (working capital build in high-volume year). 5yr: FY2020 $26.4m to FY2025 $75.0m = 23.3% - includes cyclical recovery. 4yr: FY2021 $41.6m to FY2025 $75.0m = 15.9% - more stable. FCF growth elevated by cyclical recovery from FY2023 trough.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Equity 5yr CAGR (10.5%) selected as primary metric per value investing convention - it captures through-cycle value creation including the FY2023 loss year impact on retained earnings. The FCF 5yr CAGR of 23.3% is elevated by recovery from cyclone year. Revenue 5yr CAGR of 11.8% closely corroborates the equity CAGR. EPS 5yr CAGR of 7.9% is slightly lower due to share dilution and tax headwinds. No single metric is used mechanically given the extreme cyclicality - scenario growth rates reflect thoughtful judgment about through-cycle performance.
historical_growth.divergence_note: No divergence warning triggered. Equity 5yr CAGR (10.5%), revenue 5yr CAGR (11.8%) and EPS 5yr CAGR (7.9%) are all within 15% of each other, indicating consistent value creation. The FCF 5yr CAGR of 23.3% is elevated by cyclical recovery but the 4yr CAGR (15.9%) is more representative.

base.growth_rationale: FY2025 was a record year ($75m FCF). Base case assumes modest Year 1 growth of 5% reflecting uncertainty about FY2026 season (management gave no volume guidance, noting 'too early to indicate'). Years 2-3 accelerate to 7% as automation investments at Kerikeri and Huka Pak deliver structural cost benefits and Raukokore orchard volumes ramp. Years 4-5 decelerate to 5-6% as industry approaches the Zespri 236m tray target, representing a through-cycle growth rate aligned with NZ kiwifruit volume expansion targets (+10% to 2030 = ~2% pa compounded with operating leverage).
base.fcf_margin_rationale: FY2025 FCF/Revenue = 75.0/440.0 = 17.0%. This is marginally above the FY2024 ratio (16.0%) reflecting EBITDA margin expansion from automation and volume leverage. Base case holds this flat assuming cost inflation (labour, electricity, packaging) offsets automation gains at steady state.
base.wacc_rationale: Components: NZ 10-yr risk-free rate 4.2% + beta-adjusted equity risk premium (beta ~1.1 x 7.0% ERP = 7.7%) + small-cap NZX premium 1.5% + operational cyclicality/weather premium 1.5% - financial leverage benefit (net debt/EBITDA now ~1.0x, down from 2.3x) ~3.9% = approximately 11.0%. Lower than prior 11% model justified by balance sheet improvement (net debt down 42% from $172m peak to $100m).
base.terminal_growth_rationale: Conservative terminal growth reflecting mature NZ kiwifruit industry with modest long-term volume expansion. Below NZ long-run GDP growth of 2.5-3% given agricultural cyclicality and increasing weather risk over the terminal period. Zespri's 10% industry volume growth to 2030 provides medium-term support, but beyond that, growth will moderate.

bull.growth_rationale: Bull case: FY2026 Zespri season is another record (industry tracking toward 215-220m trays), Reemoon automation installations deliver ahead of expectations, Australian orchards enter production and contribute materially, and debt reduction accelerates ROIC. Starting at 10% Year 1 reflects strong industry momentum and 47m tray base expanding toward 50m+ with new grower supply. Growth decelerates naturally to 7% by Year 5 as industry approaches maturity.
bull.fcf_margin_rationale: Automation delivers meaningful per-tray cost reduction (building on FY2024's 19% cost-per-tray reduction). Higher volumes absorb fixed costs more efficiently. FCF margin expansion from 17% to 18.5% driven by Reemoon installations reducing labour and per-unit energy costs.
bull.wacc_rationale: Lower risk premium as balance sheet strengthens toward $70-80m net debt, dividend is established and growing, automation de-risks operational execution, and market re-rates the business as a quality agricultural infrastructure company rather than a pure cyclical. NZ OCR continues to normalise, reducing the risk-free rate component.
bull.terminal_growth_rationale: Industry continues moderate expansion beyond Zespri's current plan, Seeka gains market share through consolidation of smaller operators, and Australian operations become a material earnings contributor warranting slightly higher terminal growth.

bear.growth_rationale: Bear case: FY2026 is a poor growing season (inadequate winter chill, drought, or cyclone event in Bay of Plenty). A 25% FCF decline returns Seeka toward $55-60m OCF - consistent with a season producing approximately 38-40m trays at reduced per-tray margins from fixed cost absorption. Years 2-4 see gradual recovery at 4-5% pa as industry normalises, but structural headwinds (climate change, Northern Hemisphere SunGold competition) limit growth to 4% by Year 5.
bear.fcf_margin_rationale: Poor season compresses FCF margin as fixed costs (650+ permanent staff, 12 packhouses, debt service) are spread over lower volumes. FY2023 demonstrated FCF collapse from volume loss. Margin of 14.5% represents a soft season recovery level, above the near-zero FCF of FY2023 but materially below peak.
bear.wacc_rationale: Higher risk premium reflecting volume uncertainty, potential covenant stress if debt reduction stalls, climate risk materialising, and re-rating risk if the market questions earnings sustainability. Banking covenants (3.25x leverage, 2.0x interest cover) could be stressed in a poor season.
bear.terminal_growth_rationale: Structural headwinds limit terminal growth: climate change increases growing risk in the Bay of Plenty, Northern Hemisphere SunGold competition moderates per-tray returns over time, and a mature NZ industry with limited new orchard area available constrains volume expansion beyond 2030.

base.interpretation: Base case terminal value of $28.76/share supports an entry price of $14.30 to achieve 15% CAGR over 5 years. Current price of $5.23 is 64% below this entry price.

bull.interpretation: Bull case terminal value of $43.05/share supports an entry price of $21.40. Current price of $5.23 is 76% below this level.

bear.interpretation: Even in the bear case, terminal value of $15.48/share supports an entry price of $7.70. Current price of $5.23 is 32% below even the bear case entry price.

sensitivity.note: Intrinsic value per share (NZD) across WACC and terminal growth combinations. Uses base case FCF projections. Rows = WACC (low to high), Columns = terminal growth (low to high).

probability_weighted.rationale: Equal 25% weight for bull and bear reflects high earnings cyclicality - the business can genuinely produce either exceptional years (FY2025 record) or loss years (FY2023). Base case at 50% reflects the most likely path of industry growth continuing through the cycle.

key_metrics_summary.note: P/E of 6.9x on record FY2025 earnings. EV/EBITDA of 3.3x is very low for a business with growing volumes and improving margins. FCF yield of 34.1% (based on $75m OCF / $220m market cap) is exceptional. Price/Book of 0.76x suggests stock trades below liquidation value of assets.

key_assumptions.fcf_definition: Operating Cash Flow used as Free Cash Flow proxy. Management has guided that growth capex is held to maintenance levels given the existing >50 million tray post-harvest capacity. FY2025 OCF estimated at $75m based on EBITDA $96m less estimated cash tax $12m and cash interest $9m.
key_assumptions.mid_cycle_consideration: FY2025 was a record year (47.1m trays, record EBITDA, record NPBT). Projections deliberately start modestly at 5% growth to reflect uncertainty about the 2026 season and mean-reversion risk. The bear case Y1 decline of 25% reflects the genuine probability of a poor growing year (FY2023 saw OCF collapse to $2.7m).
key_assumptions.wacc_components: Base: NZ 10-yr risk-free 4.2% + beta-adjusted ERP (1.1 x 7.0%) + small-cap premium 1.5% + cyclical/weather premium 1.5% - leverage benefit ~3.9% = 11.0%. Bull: 9.5% reflecting balance sheet improvement. Bear: 12.5% reflecting covenant stress risk.
key_assumptions.net_debt: Net bank debt of $100.3m confirmed at 31 December 2025. Down from $172m peak (2023), $137m (2024). Banking facility is $201m sustainability-linked revolving credit. Strong seasonal cash generation typically repays the facility meaningfully in H2.
key_assumptions.shares_outstanding: 42.08 million shares at H1-2025. Slight DRP dilution expected (2% discount) from dividend reinvestment. No material share issuance expected.
key_assumptions.nz_dollar: All values in New Zealand dollars. NZX-listed small-cap stock.
key_assumptions.terminal_value_significance: Base case: terminal value is 68.7% of enterprise value - typical for DCF but underscores sensitivity to WACC and terminal growth assumptions. Sensitivity matrix shows IV ranges from $16.44 to $35.00 across reasonable WACC and terminal growth combinations - even the most conservative scenario (13% WACC, 1.5% terminal growth) implies $16.44/share vs $5.23 current price.

strengths: Updated with FY2025 actuals (record EBITDA $96m, NPBT $48m, EPS $0.76, net debt $100.3m)
Equity 5yr CAGR (10.5%) closely aligned with revenue 5yr CAGR (11.8%) - no divergence
Base case growth rates (5-7%) are deliberately conservative vs historical equity CAGR (10.5%)
WACC of 11% appropriately reflects NZ small-cap, cyclical business, and weather dependency
Bear case Y1 decline of 25% stress-tests a genuine poor season scenario
All five WACC x terminal growth combinations in the sensitivity matrix show IV well above current price
Net debt down 42% from peak - materially reduces financial risk vs prior model
limitations: FY2025 is a peak year - base FCF of $75m may overstate mid-cycle FCF (historical midpoint is closer to $40-50m)
OCF used as FCF proxy - actual capex for 2026 Reemoon automation may reduce FCF by $5-10m in Year 1
Extreme cyclicality makes linear projections unreliable - actual results will be highly volatile year-to-year
Terminal value represents 68.7% of base case EV - standard DCF limitation for growing businesses
No NZ market consensus exists (thinly traded small-cap) to validate against
dcf_quality_assessment.confidence_level: Moderate-High. Even the most conservative sensitivity scenario ($16.44/share at 13% WACC, 1.5% terminal growth) implies 214% upside. The margin of safety at current price ($5.23) is exceptional across all scenarios. Key risk is that the market is correctly pricing in a near-term poor season followed by structural headwinds.

investment_context.valuation_at_current_price: At $5.23, Seeka trades at: 6.9x FY2025 earnings, 3.3x EV/EBITDA, 0.76x book value, 34% FCF yield. These metrics imply the market is pricing in either a structural earnings decline or assigns negligible terminal value. The probability-weighted IV of $22.54 implies 330% upside. Even the bear case intrinsic value of $11.38 implies 117% upside from current levels.

Interest rate trajectory affecting WACC and debt service costs

methodology_notes.base_year: FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025) - most recent full year with confirmed actuals
methodology_notes.fcf_calculation: OCF used as FCF proxy based on management guidance that growth capex is held to maintenance. Automation investments (Reemoon) are funded from existing capex budget and banking facility rather than incremental FCF draw.
methodology_notes.cyclicality_adjustment: Bear case Year 1 represents a poor-but-not-extreme season (25% FCF decline). FY2023 extreme case would show near-zero FCF. The model does not attempt to predict timing of poor seasons but scenario weights (25% bear) acknowledge meaningful probability.
methodology_notes.growth_rate_philosophy: Base case growth rates (5-7%) are set below the historical equity CAGR (10.5%) and well below revenue CAGR (11.8%) to account for: (a) FY2025 being a peak year, (b) seasonal volatility averaging effects, and (c) increasing weather risk over the projection period.
methodology_notes.valuation_date: 9 March 2026. Stock price NZ$5.23 fetched from Yahoo Finance.
